title: Renewal Readiness: Spotlight Facilitator Kit
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, facilitator-focused kit for running a 60–75 minute 'Renewal Readiness Spotlight' QBR built to surface renewal momentum, unblock obstacles, and land concrete decisions. Designed for mid-market and strategic accounts where renewal conversations need both evidence and a decision path.

Intended audience:
- CSM (lead facilitator)
- Solutions engineer or AM (subject matter)
- Customer champion(s) and procurement (stakeholder invite)

Topline outcomes (what we want at close):
1) Renewal posture decision: Renew / Risk / Requires follow-up (owner + due date)
2) 2–3 prioritized runway items that materially increase renewal likelihood (owner + due date)
3) Agreed enablement ask from our side (credits, POC, exec intro) or next-step cadence

Pre-meeting prep (checklist for facilitator — 48–72h):
- Pull last 90d usage: token counts, peak latency, error rate. (attach screenshot)
- Adoption highlights: top 3 feature adopters, top 3 stalled flows, notable admin churn
- Support signal snapshot: open sev2/3 tickets, recent escalations, average time-to-resolution last 30d
- Cost/efficiency note: current per-call cost and any recent optimization (batching, quantization) suggestions from Engineering
- Renewal history + commercial posture: current renewal date, term length, commercial owner, previous NRR/ARR trends
- Invite pre-reads: one-pager of highlights (2 slides), one-pager of risks (1 slide) — send 72h before
- Slack ping customer champion night-before with 3 bullet agenda and ask to bring any procurement constraints

Meeting agenda (60–75m):
0–5m  Quick check-in and objectives (facilitator opening script below)
5–20m  Spotlight: wins and usage signal (customer briefly shares top product outcomes)
20–35m Show the data: usage, errors, cost, adoption funnel (CS presents) — surface anomalies and two hypotheses
35–50m Risk & unblock workshop (facilitated): map top 3 blockers, propose mitigations, timebox decisions
50–60m Decision checkpoint: apply the Micro-Decision Rubric (see below) per blocker
60–70m Commercial & enablement alignment: confirm renewal stance or agree next-step cadence
70–75m Close: confirm owners, timelines, and follow-up email draft

Facilitator script (snippets you can paste into meeting chat or say aloud):
- Opening: "Thanks all — today our goal is to confirm whether we have the runway to move to renewal or what precise blockers remain. We’ll be decision-oriented and document owners for every next step."
- Spotlight intro: "Can you share the single biggest outcome you need from Redwood in the next 90 days? We’ll use that as our north star for decisions."
- Data framing: "We’re showing both broad usage and a couple of outliers — my working hypotheses are X and Y; I want your read and then we’ll test mitigations."
- Redirecting to decisions: "We’ve mapped three options for resolving this: do A, do B, or schedule a tech deep-dive. Which do you prefer and who should own it?"
- Closing: "Two quick confirmations: owner + due date for each item, and agreed date for the renewal decision checkpoint. I’ll follow up with notes and calendar invites."

Micro-Decision Rubric (quick):
- Renew: clear product fit + blockers mitigated or on track + exec sponsor present
- At-risk: product fit present but blocker(s) need >30 days or require commercial concession
- Requires follow-up: insufficient data OR technical unknowns; commit to specific exploration window (7–21 days)

Renewal Momentum Tracker (paste into meeting doc — editable):
- Renewal date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Current posture (initial): [Green/Yellow/Red]
- Key stakeholders: [names + roles]
- Top 3 blockers (ranked) + proposed mitigation + owner + due date
- Commercial ask (discount/credit/term change) + owner + decision window
- Post-meeting posture (final): [Green/Yellow/Red]

Risk & Fallback flows (if customer escalates procurement/price):
- If procurement asks for >20% discount: escalate to AM and propose time-boxed POC + NPS-based credit instead of permanent discount
- If technical gap uncovered: propose 2-week technical POC with SE support; owner = Solutions Eng; schedule within 5 business days
- If exec alignment missing: request 15-minute exec-to-exec skip-level within 7 days (offer 1–2 time slots)

Post-meeting playbook (first 14 days):
Day 0: Send summary email with decisions, owners, due dates, and calendar invites for follow-ups (CS owner)
Day 3: Drop-in sync with technical owner on mitigation progress (SE owner)
Day 7: Progress readout to champion and AM; update renewal posture (CS owner)
Day 14: Final decision checkpoint or extension request captured; escalate if still red (CS + AM)

Templates (short)
- Invite blurb (email): "We’d like to run a 60–75m Renewal Readiness Spotlight to share usage trends, surface blockers, and lock in a renewal posture. Please bring your procurement/ops rep if there are commercial constraints. Pre-reads attached."
- Follow-up summary blurb: "Thanks — attached are notes, owners, and due dates. Next sync: [date]. Please let us know if any details need correction."

Notes to facilitator (things we often forget):
- Confirm seating of exec sponsor at start (if pre-committed). If absent, surface a clear follow-up step for their sign-off.
- Keep data visuals simple: 1 slide for usage trend, 1 slide for error spikes, 1 slide for adoption funnel.
- If customer goes long on technical detail, park it to a separate deep-dive and call it out as a follow-up so decisions don’t slip.
- Use the Micro-Decision Rubric out loud to keep ambiguity from creeping in.

Open items & questions for iteration:
- Should we standardize a 2-week POC offer template (legal approval needed)?
- Can PM provide an exec-ready 1-pager for top 10 strategic accounts?
- Explore automating the Renewal Momentum Tracker from our analytics exports (engineers: is there a lightweight export we can reuse?)

Attached examples (placeholders):
- screenshot_usage_90d.png
- adoption_funnel_table.csv
- sample_followup_email.txt

-- end of kit --

(quick note: this is intentionally compact — meant to be a facilitator cheat-sheet rather than a full QBR deck. keep a copy in the account folder and mark as versioned when you iterate.)
